options.title: How Did Gold Foil and Plastic Make the First Transistor?
options.first_line: The first transistor was gold foil pressed on a plastic wedge. How did that become every chip you own?
options.first_frame: A glowing plastic wedge wrapped in gold foil descends onto a grey germanium slab on a dark lab bench, the camera pushing in as a spark of current lights the tip.

options.title: What Did the First Transistor Actually Look Like?
options.first_line: Every chip in your phone is built from one switch. What did the very first one look like?
options.first_frame: A phone's chip dissolves into a glowing grid of tiny switches, and the camera pulls back through them to land on a hand-sized gold-and-plastic contraption on a lab bench.

options.title: How Did Bell Labs Build the First Transistor by Hand?
options.first_line: At Bell Labs, two scientists built the first transistor by hand. What was it made of?
options.first_frame: A dark 1940s lab bench, a paper clip spring pressing a gold-edged plastic triangle onto a crystal, a meter needle already swinging as the camera circles.

why: It starts from the phone in the viewer's hand and asks what the first switch looked like without giving it away, while A's title already gives the answer (gold foil and plastic) and C's is about a lab the viewer never touches.
